elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) states that, if the Company terminates, it shall pay HDI “no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages” and that the Termination Payment amount is zero. Sections 4.2(b) and (c) do not create a payment because subsection (b) confirms no payment is due when the amount is zero and subsection (c) applies only “if any.”

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) expressly provides that the Company shall pay HDI no “penalty,” and fixes the relevant Termination Payment at zero.

elements.element: Any fee payable by Customer under the fallback is triggered only by Customer's early termination.
elements.evidence: No termination fee is payable at all under the rendered language, so the condition requiring a permissible fee to be limited to an early-termination trigger is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at an amount equal to three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) fixes the Termination Payment at zero. Zero is below a three-month-fee cap, and subsection (b) confirms that no payment is due when the amount is zero.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause permits no early-termination fee, penalty, or liquidated damages at all. Accordingly, there is no additional liquidated amount payable by the Company; this is more protective than allowing one sole capped amount.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred no-payment position and therefore also satisfies the less protective fallback. It preserves the term and termination mechanics and does not create an operative contradiction. It is not minimal or cleanly drafted because “the amount of which shall be zero and not an amount equal to” is redundant and awkward, while subsections (b) and (c) retain unnecessary provisions concerning a payment that can no longer arise.
